page: Vultr vc2-4c-8gb is a shared-CPU instance belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It features an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the server.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned in the lower tiers of compute and memory capabilities. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded weak results, scoring 1304.17 and 5030.23 respectively. Memory performance shows a stark contrast between cached and uncached operations; while the cached small-block read bandwidth achieved an average tier of 367.64 GB/sec, the uncached large-block read and write bandwidths fell into the weak category at 24.41 GB/sec and 19.55 GB/sec.

Real-world application benchmarks reflect these hardware constraints. The server achieved 2.63 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a static web serving throughput of 3.09 GB/sec. Software compilation with Clang scored 3144.0, and text processing on Geekbench was poor at 727.0. Given the shared CPU allocation and modest performance profile, this instance offers a highly cost-efficient solution for resource-light workloads. It is best suited for development environments, basic web serving, lightweight background tasks, and testing scenarios where dedicated CPU performance is not required.
